title: Dashboard ownership rollout cheatsheet (brainstorm)
body:
Context:
This is a lightweight working doc to propose a repeatable checklist and ownership model for shipping and maintaining observability dashboards for inference services (hosted API, dedicated pools, private). We keep hitting the same problems during rollouts: dashboards with ambiguous owners, exploding widget cardinality, noisy alerts after canary, missing trace anchors for session reconstruction, and unclear migration steps when models or routing change.

Goal:
Create a small, pragmatic playbook that teams can follow when creating or updating dashboards so they are: owned, low-noise, trace-linked, cost-conscious, and easy to verify during rollouts and post-launch. This is intentionally informal — meant for iteration.

Principles (short):
- Single owner per dashboard (not per widget) for operational questions.
- Signal-level ownership: someone owns metric correctness, naming, and data pipeline.
- Prefer low-cardinality aggregates on the main view; expose drilldowns for tenant or model-level slices.
- Instrument traces with stable anchors (session_id/request_id/model_version) for reconstruction.
- Include token-economics context (per-token cost or request-size buckets) for inference dashboards.

Proposed roles and responsibilities:
- Dashboard Owner: responsible for the dashboard lifecycle (create, review, retire), runbook linkage, and post-mortem participation.
- Signal Owner: the engineer who ensures metric instrumentation and contracts (unit semantics, cardinality, fallback semantics).
- Widget Owner: maintains a specific widget (query, threshold, query cost) and paginates drilldowns. Often the same as Signal Owner for small teams.
- Incident Liaison / RTE: during incidents, the liaison owns coordinating widget-level deep-dives and trace reconstruction.

Rollout checklist (phases):
1) Pre-rollout (PR / design review):
   - Draft dashboard layout in a private folder or dev space.
   - Define the primary SLI(s) and explicit acceptance criteria (e.g., 95th p99 latency delta < Xms).
   - Document signal owners and provenance for each metric (where it comes from, aggregation window). Reference Confluence metric-contract page.
   - Validate query cost: run the dashboard queries at expected retention/filters and capture query cost estimate.
   - Identify any high-cardinality filters (tenant/model/route) and move them to secondary drilldowns, not main view.
   - Add trace anchors to the top-level widget descriptions: session_id, request_id, user_id (PII redaction statement).
   - Add a short runbook snippet to the dashboard notes: immediate checks, fallback model, canary thresholds.

2) Rollout:
   - Smoke-check the dashboard with synthetic traffic (canary traffic) and confirm metric shapes.
   - Check sampling of traces for the relevant endpoints; ensure session reconstruction works end-to-end.
   - Flag any alerts that fire during canary; tune thresholds before broad rollout.
   - Confirm the dashboard owner is on rotation/PD pager or has a delegate during the first 72h.

3) Post-rollout (2–4 weeks):
   - Collect false-positive alert counts and adjust SLI thresholds or sampling.
   - Verify data continuity across model version rollouts (compare vN vs vN-1 baselines).
   - Archive or prune unused widgets (>=90% unseen by team in last 30 days).
   - Finalize ownership in the team roster and link to Signal Inventory.

Essential Widgets / Metrics (suggested starter set):
- Request throughput (rps) by route / global
- 95th/99th latency (token completion & server processing) for top routes
- KV cache hit rate (global and per-model cluster)
- Mean/median batch size and batching latency distribution
- Model fallback / error rate and error taxonomy (model OOM, timeout, inference error)
- Token consumption per-request bucket (0-64, 65-256, >256) and per-tenant cost estimate
- Cold-cache rate and cache warm-up time percentiles
- Queue depth / scheduling backlog for dedicated pools
- Synthetic probe success rate (canary) with trace links attached

Trace anchoring and sampling guidance (practical):
- Anchor traces with a canonical request_id that persists across service hops and model routing. Put the request_id in the dashboard widget tooltip for quick copy-paste into trace UI.
- Store model_version and route as span tags to make model-level filtering cheap.
- Use tiered sampling: 0.1% of all traffic kept full-trace, 10% of failed/latency-exceeding requests kept full-trace, and 100% of synthetic canary traces.
- Redact or hash any PII (user email/user id) at ingestion; keep original only in ephemeral debug retention if strictly necessary and audited.

Low-cardinality and cost-aware design tips:
- Prefer aggregated time-series and use precomputed rollups for tenant-level slices when possible.
- Move high-cardinality breakdowns to dedicated drilldown dashboards that are not queried by default.
- Use compact quantiles (TDigest or HDR) rather than many percentile widgets to reduce storage/query cost.
- Limit default time-range to 6h for frequently-opened dashboards; provide a one-click 30d view for trend analysis.

Quick wins / experiments to try:
- Auto-generate trace links in hover tooltips for top 5 slowest requests in a time bucket.
- Add a "cost per 1000 requests" widget derived from token buckets to make economic tradeoffs visible.
- Tiny feedback button on dashboards for operators to mark a widget as noisy, with automated tagging and follow-up.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-up):
- Should dashboard ownership live in the same code review flow as metrics instrumentation PRs? (pros: review context; cons: scope creep)
- How to enforce signal ownership in the org: lightweight SCC (signal change check) vs. formal gating?
- What retention-levels are appropriate for full traces for private deployments with compliance constraints?

Immediate next steps / action items (owners):
- Aisha: draft a lightweight ownership annotation template and add to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-OBS-1423).
- Miguel: prototype trace-link hover for one widget (GH-PR-4892).
- Priya: run query-cost report for standard dashboard templates and share numbers by 2026-03-05 (JIRA-OBS-314).
- Lena: schedule a 45m sync with product-hosted-api and SRE to align on alert thresholds.

Notes / links:
- Metric contract templates: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/metric-contracts-templates
- Example runbook snippet (copy/paste): Immediate checks: 1) check queue depth 2) check cache hit rate 3) check fallbacks.
- Slack channel for follow-up: #observability-play

This doc is intentionally rough. Aim: convert into a one-page dashboard checklist + a tiny annotation template that can be dropped into dashboard descriptions.

Unresolved: the exact sampling fraction we should standardize on for hosted vs private (depends on compliance). Put on next week's obs sync agenda.
